findings.test: api › api/security.spec.ts › API — Security headers on every audited page › Content-Security-Policy restricts where scripts load from
findings.summary: The Content-Security-Policy only sets `frame-ancestors 'self'`. With no `script-src` or `default-src` it does not limit where scripts load from, so it gives no protection against injected scripts (XSS). Same header on every page, search, 404 and REST response. Seen 2026-11-15; reproduce with `curl -sI https://uptichospitality.com/ | grep -i content-security-policy`

findings.remediation: Start with `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` listing the script hosts the site really uses (`'self'`, analytics), review the reports for a week, then enforce it. Avoid `'unsafe-inline'`; use nonces for inline scripts

findings.test: api › api/security.spec.ts › API — Security headers on every audited page › responses do not advertise server software versions
findings.summary: Every response PHP generates (pages, search, 404, REST API) carries `X-Powered-By: PHP/8.3.36`, telling anyone the exact PHP version to look up vulnerabilities for. Static files from the CDN do not. Seen 2026-11-15; reproduce with `curl -sI https://uptichospitality.com/ | grep -i x-powered-by`

findings.test: desktop › accessibility.spec.ts › Accessibility — Article: Independent Hotels › keyboard: Tab moves through the page and every stop shows focus
findings.summary: The search field above the footer shows no focus indicator: when focused by keyboard, the input's computed `outline-style` is `none`, and nothing else on the input, its wrapper or the form (border, shadow, background) changes, so keyboard users cannot see where they are (WCAG 2.4.7). Checked by hand on 2026-11-15 (computed styles and a screenshot): focused and unfocused look the same apart from the text caret. Which stylesheet removes the outline was not traced

findings.remediation: Add a focus style to the Search block, e.g. `.wp-block-search__inside-wrapper:focus-within { outline: 2px solid #1F3A2E; outline-offset: 2px; }`
